newsitem.title: CHINA: Winsan offers 250 mln shrs at HK$2.01/shr in IPO.
newsitem.headline: Winsan offers 250 mln shrs at HK$2.01/shr in IPO.

text.p: Chinese property firm Winsan (China) Investment Group Co Ltd said on Thursday it is offering 250 million new shares, or 25 percent of its enlarged share capital, at HK$2.01 each in an initial public offering (IPO).

The issue price represents a price earnings multiple of 9.57 times on a proforma fully-diluted basis and a 30.93 percent discount to net asset value (NAV) per share of HK$2.91 after provisions for the deferred taxation on the evaluation surplus.
The IPO will run from July 11 to 16 and dealing in the company shares is expected to begin on July 25.
China Development Finance Co (Hong Kong) Ltd is the sponsor of the issue.
Net proceeds of about HK$475.5 million after expenses will mainly be used to fund its development projects in Chinese cities of Shanghai, Beijing, Fuzhou, Suzhou, and Nanjing.
The balance will be used for general working capital.
Bank of China Group Investment Ltd, Beijing Enterprises Holdings Ltd, and Shanghai Industrial Holdings Ltd will each take one percent or 10 million shares of the company's enlarged shares capital.
Winsan (China) is a property investor and developer in the region of Yangze River Delta and Fuzhou. Residential property comprises a major portion of its portfolio.
The properties developed by the company are targeted at China domestic consumers, mainly Chinese enterprises.
The company said properties sold to Chinese enterrpises accounted about 85 percent of its turnover for the year ended December 1996.
It said it has interests in seven properties which were under development and would provide a total gross floor area (GFA) of about 247,032 square metres.
It also had interests in eight properties which are held for future developments. The estimated gross floor area of the properties is about 1.34 million square metres.
The firm said it has total net asset value of over HK$2.9 billion with property development projects Fuzhou, Shanghai, Nanjing, Suzhou and Beijing.
About 87 percent of the company's residential flats has been brought by Chinese enterprises for allocation to their staff, while the other 13 percent has been taken by retail buyers.

The company forecast profit after taxation and minority interests of not less than HK$195 million for the year ending in December 1997, up from HK$25.1 million in 1996 and HK$18.9 million in 1995 and HK$19.8 million in 1994.
Its total revenue was HK$188.46 million in 1996, up from HK$128.68 million in 1995 and HK$104.91 million in 1994.
